fixtures.basis: Sioux Falls's plumbing ordinance rewrites UPC Section 422.1 so that the minimum number of fixtures comes from Chapter 29 and Table 2902.1 of the International Building Code, not from UPC Table 422.1, and does not adopt UPC 422.2 to 422.5. The city's building code ordinance (No. 77-26) prints Table 2902.1 in full and adds Sections 2902.1.4 (urinals), 2902.2 (separate rooms), 2903.1.4 and 2903.1.5 (compartments and urinal partitions). Both read in the city's own PDFs.

amendment.text: (1) Fixture numbers come from the building code's Table 2902.1: office (business) 1 toilet per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 beyond, for each sex; restaurant 1 per 75; school 1 per 50; shop (mercantile) 1 per 500. (2) Occupants are split 50 percent male, 50 percent female unless information submitted shows otherwise. (3) One fixture serves the stated number of people or any fraction of it. (4) Urinals are optional and may replace not more than 67 percent of the required toilets in a toilet room. (5) Separate rooms for each sex are not required at 15 or fewer occupants in total, in a mercantile occupancy of 100 or fewer, or in a business or storage occupancy of 25 or fewer; nor where single-user rooms are provided, nor where a room is designed for all persons with each toilet in a compartment and each urinal in a partitioned area. (6) The UPC's own separate-facilities section (422.2), with its 10 and 50 occupant exceptions, is not adopted by the city.
amendment.quote: 422.1 Fixture Count.* Plumbing fixtures may be provided for the type of building occupancy and in the minimum number in accordance with Chapter 29 and Table 2902.1 of the International Building Code. The total occupant load and occupancy classification shall be determined in accordance with the building code. The minimum number of fixtures shall be calculated at 50 percent male and 50 percent female based on the total occupant load. Where information submitted indicates a difference in distribution of the sexes, such information shall be used in order to determine the number of fixtures for each sex. Once the occupancy load and occupancy are determined, Table 2902.1 of the International Building Code shall be applied to determine the minimum number of plumbing fixtures required. 422.2 Separate Facilities. Not adopted by city. 422.3 Fixture Requirements for Special Occupancies. Not adopted by city. 422.4 Toilet Facilities Serving Employees and Customers. Not adopted by city. [...] 422.5 Toilet Facilities for Workers. Not adopted by city.

office.quote: Buildings for the transaction of business, nonmedical professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses: [water closets] 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

table_rows.rounding_quote: a. The fixtures shown are based on one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction of the number of persons indicated. The number of occupants shall be determined by this code.
table_rows.urinal_quote: 2902.1.4 Substitution for water closets. In a toilet room or bathroom, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets.
table_rows.separate_rooms_quote: [P] 2902.2 Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: 1. Separate facilities shall not be required for dwelling units and sleeping units. 2. Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. 3. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. 4. Separate facilities shall not be required in business or storage occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer. 5. Separate facilities shall not be required to be designated by sex where single-user toilets rooms are provided in accordance with Section 2902.1.2. 6. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by all persons regardless of sex and privacy is provided for water closets in accordance with Section 2903.1.4 and for urinals in accordance with Section 2903.1.5.
table_rows.urinal_partition_quote: 2903.1.5 Urinal partitions. Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy. The horizontal dimension between walls or partitions at each urinal shall be not less than 30 inches (762 mm). The walls or partitions shall begin at a height not greater than 12 inches (305 mm) from and extend not less than 60 inches (1,524 mm) above the finished floor surface.
table_rows.compartment_quote: 2903.1.4 Water closet compartment. Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy.

state_conflict.note: The state pack's table (UPC Table 422.1: more women's toilets, required urinals) is the State Plumbing Code's. SDCL 36-25-16 lets a city set its own plumbing standards 'provided that the standards as contained in such ordinances meet the minimum standards of the State Plumbing Code'. The city's table gives lower numbers than the state's in most of the worked examples (office of 400: 5 women's toilets against 8; no required urinals). The city's booklet says most of its amendments mirror the state's, but marks 422.1 as modified locally. Which table Sioux Falls plan review applies in practice, and how the city squares it with 36-25-16, was not found in writing: phone item.

worked_examples.how: 50 occupants split in half = 25 of each sex. Table 2902.1 at 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder: 1 toilet(s) for each sex (any fraction counts as one fixture). Urinals are optional: not more than 67 percent of 1, so up to 0. Separate rooms are waived only at 25 occupants or fewer in a business occupancy, so 50 occupants still need two rooms.

100 occupants split in half = 50 of each sex. Table 2902.1 at 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder: 2 toilet(s) for each sex (any fraction counts as one fixture). Urinals are optional: not more than 67 percent of 2, so up to 1.

200 occupants split in half = 100 of each sex. Table 2902.1 at 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder: 3 toilet(s) for each sex (any fraction counts as one fixture). Urinals are optional: not more than 67 percent of 3, so up to 2.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Sioux Falls job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the city rules and 6.2% sales tax.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Sioux Falls offices, schools, clinics and warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Sioux Falls's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Sioux Falls sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Sioux Falls extras:** the city applies a national accessibility standard that goes further than the federal rules in two details: an accessible stall needs an 18 inch vertical grab bar beside the toilet as well as the horizontal one, and the partitions of a wheelchair stall need 12 inches of toe room above the floor instead of 9. The plumbing rules also name a security standard for toilet partitions and urinal screens, so ask your plan reviewer whether it applies to your project.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. In a private building, a shared all-gender room may take the place of separate men's and women's rooms if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and every urinal has its own partitioned area. In public schools and in buildings owned, leased or occupied by the state, a county or a city, South Dakota law requires restrooms for more than one person to be designated for females only or males only.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Sioux Falls requires a permit to alter a building unless the work is on its exempt list, and the building official may exempt minor work. The list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops, and similar finish work" and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high, but it doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask Sioux Falls Building Services at 605-367-8670 whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Sioux Falls counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. The city's plumbing ordinance takes the numbers from the table in its building rules. Urinals are optional: they may take the place of up to 67 percent of the toilets a men's room needs, each with a screen on both sides, so the table shows men's toilets as stalls.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. An office or warehouse designed for 25 people or fewer, a shop designed for 100 or fewer and any building designed for 15 or fewer doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. South Dakota's statewide plumbing rules use a different table, with more women's toilets and required urinals, and state law says a city's plumbing rules must meet the state's minimum. Ask Sioux Falls Building Services which numbers your plans are reviewed against.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Sioux Falls's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 25. Your architect or Sioux Falls Building Services sets the final number.
skip_state_sources: Building codes, floor area per person
page.install_rule: Sioux Falls does not license commercial building contractors. The city reviews plans and issues permits for commercial projects. South Dakota has no state contractor license for this work, but contractors need a state contractor's tax license from the Department of Revenue. Confirm what your project needs with Sioux Falls Building Services. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Sioux Falls does not license commercial building contractors, and a contractor in South Dakota needs a state contractor's tax license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** South Dakota has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on work paid for with federal money, where federal law sets it by county. For a carpenter on building work in Minnehaha County that is $17.61 an hour plus $8.53 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6.2% in Sioux Falls: 4.2% state and 2% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals and medical offices:** stainless steel or phenolic in public restrooms that are cleaned many times a day.

notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether replacing or adding toilet partitions needs a Sioux Falls permit (Building Services, 605-367-8670, BuildingPermits@siouxfalls.gov).

To confirm by phone: which toilet table Sioux Falls plan review applies. The city's plumbing ordinance points to the building code's table (lower numbers, urinals optional), while the statewide plumbing rules keep a table with more women's toilets and required urinals and SDCL 36-25-16 requires city plumbing standards to meet the state's minimum (Plumbing Inspection Manager, 605-367-8693; South Dakota Plumbing Commission, 605-773-3429).

The city's plumbing ordinance booklet gives the approval date (January 27, 2026) but no ordinance number or effective date, and the building ordinance read (No. 77-26, effective October 8, 2026) restates an adoption that applies from July 1, 2026: check both on the city code at codelibrary.amlegal.com in a browser (it refuses automated access).

The fire-test section, the 50/50 and single-user sign sections of the building code and the accessibility standard's two details were read on UpCodes, not on ICC's site; the fire-test section says 'used as an interior finish' and doesn't name toilet partitions.

The federal carpenter rate for Minnehaha County ($17.61 plus $8.53) dates from a 2012 survey; drywall hanging and metal stud work has a separate, higher rate ($36.34 plus $17.15) that doesn't cover partition installation as classified.
The state sales tax rate is set to return to 4.5% on July 1, 2027, which would make Sioux Falls 6.5%: update the sales tax bullet then.
